title: What is known about 1RB0LD_1RC0RD_1LA0RC_1RE1LB_1LF0LA_---0LE
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LD_1RC0RD_1LA0RC_1RE1LB_1LF0LA_---0LE.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Each lap copies the tape 5 cells further left, and all change happens in an irregular zone at the right end where the lap turns. Both sweeps are proved in Lean as transducers (the right sweep over any accepted token list, the left sweep over blocks of every length from two of its three states); no halt in the first 2·109 steps (C) and 107 (Lean, native_decide). The wall-carry signature that suggested the busycoq #115 method is an artefact of the copying.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 29,507 cells have been visited and 17,521 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Two shift rules
claims.text: Rightward, C zigzags across 1 0 1 words, rewriting each into 1 1 0 in 7 steps (sweep_right); leftward, A crosses 1 1 0 words, rewriting each into 1 0 0 (sweep_left_A); for every n and every surrounding tape.

claims.title: The right sweep is a transducer on tokens
claims.text: Write the tape as tokens x = 1 0, y = 1 1 0, u = 1 0 0, v = 1 1 0 0. Going right, the head is between tokens in one of four scanner states (a machine state with a fixed word on its left). Ten crossings are proved for every tape on both sides (rule_sound), and pass_sound proves, by induction on the list, that the machine crosses any token list for which every token has a rule, leaving blocks 1^(2k) 0 behind.

claims.title: The left sweep counts mod 3
claims.text: Going left, the head reads the blocks 1^(2k) 0 back and writes tokens. From two of its three states (L0, D; L2, B) the crossing of a block is proved for every k, and the next state depends only on k mod 3 (six theorems, for every k and every tape on both sides). The third state (L1, A) first makes an 11-cell trip right over the tokens it has just written; its crossings are not proved yet.

claims.title: No halt in the first 2·10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: c/laps.c runs 2·109 steps (8,281 laps) without a halt.

claims.title: Each lap copies the tape
claims.text: Read from its own left end, the tape after a lap equals the tape before it except within the last 5 to 469 cells before the turning point (median 32, over 2,614 laps to 2·10<sup>8</sup> steps). The left end moves 5 cells left per lap; the turning point stays between cells -659 and +228 of the start (2·10<sup>9</sup> steps), so the body left of it is an inert record and all change happens in the zone at the right end.

claims.title: The turn is a nested excursion
claims.text: When the right sweep, in state E, meets u, the head turns left into the blocks it has just written. In 3·108 steps 1,913 such excursions came back right after 10 to 200 cells (the sweep goes on in state C) and 3,097 ran to the left end and ended the lap. Which one happens depends on the blocks to the left, not on the tokens to the right.

claims.title: The wall-carry signature is an artefact
claims.text: The 26 November screen for the busycoq #115-#119 method flagged values {2, 5, 8} behind the wall word 7 7 1 1 2. Each occurs exactly once per lap (2,910 times each in 3·107 steps): they are the steps of one leftward zigzag through a 1^8 block in the copied body, not a carry returned from the far end.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. A halt needs the leftward E/F zigzag to meet two 0s in the wrong phase, which the proved crossings never do; the open part is which token words the zone at the right end can hold, and the excursions that decide where each lap turns.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine sweeps back and forth, and each lap copies the whole tape five cells further left, unchanged. Everything that happens, happens in a small irregular zone at the right end, where the lap turns. Both sweeps are proved in Lean as simple transducers; the zone is the open part.

facts.text: No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The right sweep (4 states) and two of the left sweep's 3 states, proved for every length.
Each lap copies the tape this far left; only the zone changes.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.499). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).
After 109 steps the tape spans 29,507 cells (21,488 left of the start, 228 right), with a density of 1s of 0.594.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Each lap copies the tape
html: A lap runs from the left end of the tape to a turning point and back. Compare the tape before and after a lap, each read from its own left end: they are the same, cell for cell, except in the last few dozen cells before the turning point (5 to 469 cells, median 32, over 2,614 laps). The left end moves 5 cells left per lap, so the whole stretch left of the turning point is moved 5 cells left, unchanged.

The turning point itself does not move with it: it stays between cells -659 and +228 of the start. So the picture is a conveyor belt. A zone of a few hundred cells at the right end, fixed in place, does all the work; the body to its left is an inert record that the head copies on every lap. Laps get longer as the body grows, which is why the left side grows like the square root of the step count.

sections.heading: Two transducers
html: At the start of a lap the tape is a word over four tokens: x = 1 0, y = 1 1 0, u = 1 0 0, v = 1 1 0 0. Going right, the head crosses one token at a time. Between tokens it is in one of four scanner states: D0, D1, E, C. From a D state, x and y keep it in D and v moves it to E; from E, x keeps E and y returns to D; from C, x gives D and u gives E. Behind itself the head leaves blocks 1^(2k) 0. Lean proves the ten crossings and, by induction on the list, the sweep over any token list built from them (lean/RightPass.lean).

Going left, the head reads the blocks back and writes tokens again. It has three states, and the next one depends on the block length mod 3: from L0, a block 1^(2k) gives L0, L1, L2 for k = 1, 2, 3 (mod 3); from L2 it gives L2, L0, L1. Lean proves these six crossings for every k (lean/LeftPass.lean). The third state makes a short trip right over the tokens it has just written, and is not proved yet.

sections.heading: Where the lap turns
html: The right sweep stops being simple when, in state E, it meets a u. Then the head turns left into the blocks it has just written. Sometimes this excursion comes back after 10 to 200 cells and the sweep carries on to the right; sometimes it runs all the way to the left end and the lap is over. Which one happens depends on the blocks to the left. In 3·108 steps, 1,913 excursions came back and 3,097 ended a lap.

The zone where this happens looks irregular, with runs of up to 15 u in a row. Its right end stopped growing at cell 228 after lap 2,578; since then it has grown at its left edge instead. The busycoq proofs of PRs 115 to 119 needed only a carry with three values coming back from each sweep. Here the left sweep does count mod 3, but where each lap turns is decided by nested excursions, and nobody has described what the zone can hold.

sections.heading: Where it could halt
html: The halting transition is F reading 0. F is entered only from E reading 0, and E from D reading 0 or from F reading 1: going left, E and F alternate across 0 1 pairs. The machine halts only if that zigzag meets two 0s in a row in the wrong phase. The blocks the right sweep writes have single 0s, and none of the proved crossings halts, so the danger is in the zone.

sections.heading: What is proved
html: Lean, kernel: the halting configurations and no halt in 10,000 steps (lean/Blank.lean); the shift rules sweep_right and sweep_left_A (lean/Passes.lean); the right sweep as a transducer on tokens with a theorem for every token list it accepts (lean/RightPass.lean); six block crossings of the left sweep for every length (lean/LeftPass.lean). Lean, native_decide: no halt in 107 steps. C: no halt in 2·109 steps. The copying, the excursions and the zone are measurements.

family: conveyor: each lap copies the tape 5 cells left; an irregular zone at the right end
summary: Each lap copies the tape 5 cells further left; the change happens in an irregular zone at the right end, where nested left excursions decide the turn. Right and left sweeps proved as transducers in Lean; open.
